messages:
Riya (oncall): Noticed recurring p95 blips on text-generate during partner traffic bursts at ~02:30 UTC. Seems similar to prior cache warmup incidents. Opening thread to decide SLO treatment and owners.

Evan: I see the traces. Preproc node CPU + KV cache miss rate spike. Multi-tenant burst from a marketing partner.

Claire: If it's partner-driven, can we throttle at the edge or do a temporary SLO window? Prefer throttle + short SLO window.

Riya (oncall): Proposal: short SLO window p95 350ms -> 500ms for 24h, mark as "operational override", exclude from monthly burn. Edge soft-throttle for partner keys as immediate mitigation. Thoughts?

Evan: I'll take the throttle rule (burst=5, rate=2r/s) and add a cache-hit panel. ETA: 3h.

Claire: I'll post the status note and update SLO dashboard. Add Dedicated opt-out flag. ETA: 1h.

Riya (oncall): Infra-Bot, please create follow-up ticket and assign: throttle (Evan), SLO comms (Claire), dashboard (Evan).

Infra-Bot: Created REDW-4991 with subtasks REDW-4992 (edge-throttle) -> Evan, REDW-4993 (SLO update & status) -> Claire, REDW-4994 (cache panel) -> Evan. Due dates set.

Evan: Throttle pushed to canary; monitoring queue depth.

Claire: SLO note published: https://status.redwood.dev/incidents/REDW-4991 and dashboard annotated.

Riya (oncall): Scheduling 24h check-in 3032280720. Attach thread to postmortem and track in REDW-4991. Please update tickets as you progress.

Infra-Bot: Reminder scheduled: 3032280720 - "24h SLO check-in for partner-burst latency"
